page: Vultr voc-g-2c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations reveal divergent performance characteristics. Single-core processing is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and image processing benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%, while Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput register in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with large-block read and write operations performing in the middle 50%, whereas small-block cached reads are weaker.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance, this instance offers a stable baseline for workloads that do not heavily parallelize. It is suitable for lightweight general-purpose applications, basic text processing, and small-scale single-threaded tasks. However, it is less optimal for high-throughput database operations, intensive multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale web serving due to its lower multi-core and database benchmark scores. The hardware profile represents a cost-efficient entry point for dedicated x86_64 resources without the CPU throttling risks of shared-core burstable instances.
